ai.description: This snake reaches 45–60 cm. It is reddish-brown with distinct black crossbands and a dark V-shaped head mark. It features a blunt snout and a white venter with dark lateral spots.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Abor Hills Kukri Snake is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, broad black nuchal collar that remains unbroken across the nape of the neck.
ai.habitat: The Abor Hills Kukri snake inhabits dense, humid tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests, typically found at elevations ranging from 500 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Abor Hills kukri snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice open reptile eggs, allowing it to consume the contents.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon melanozonatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon season, with hatchlings typically appearing in late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon melanozonatus* is endemic to the Eastern Himalayas, specifically recorded in Arunachal Pradesh, India, at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
